- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.25) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- When recent price history shows strong upward momentum (last 3–5 days rising >5%), model tends to over-forecast; apply downward bias to next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a spike and true outcome declines, reduce forecast by 10–15% for the following 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast deviates >10% from true outcome, apply mean reversion: adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently higher than forecast, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 10 days to account for lagged momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated positive spikes (e.g., 2+ consecutive 0.5+), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast by 5–8% for next 5 days.
